newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: Namibian stocks week-Options traded for first time.
newsitem.headline: Namibian stocks week-Options traded for first time.

text.p: Equity options were traded on the Namibian Stock Exchange for the first time last week, marking another stage in the growing sophistication of the country's capital markets.
A total of 20,000 options to buy shares in African Portland Industrial (API) were bought at five cents each.
The options give the owner the right to buy API shares at N$6.00 each on October 1 1997, compared with the share's traded price of N$5.25 last week.
Wholesaling, food, packaging and manufacturing group CIC Holdings traded 1.3 million shares during the week with the price at N$2.70 by week-end.
Namibia Breweries continued at N$2.55 with lower volumes of 21.500 shares. Nictus traded at N$1.20 and Sentra at N$4.50.
The total value of shares traded during the week was N$11 million, with a total volume of some 1.814 million shares.
The NSE Overall Index ended the week at 216.07, up from 208.13 in the previous week.
The NSE Local Index slipped to 150.20 from 152.17.
